value:
THE TERNARY-DIAMOND LEVER IS NOT FLOAT-SPECIFIC. Where target shows `cmpwi rX,0; beq ->F; b ->M; F: li rV,0; M:` and your build shows the single inverted branch `cmpwi rX,0; bne ->M; li rV,0; M:`, the residual is that your source states the zeroing as a NEGATED GUARD (`if (!c) { v = 0; }`) while the original stated it as a TERNARY (`v = c ? v : 0;`). Rewriting it as the ternary reproduces target's two-branch form exactly, on INTEGER operands.

WHY THIS NEEDS ITS OWN RECORD. claim.law.float-clamp-ternary-diamond-vs-negated-guard.20260831.v1 already carries the mechanism -- 'MWCC collapses an empty statement block but never collapses a ternary's arm block', so the ternary's empty true arm still emits its own unconditional `b` to the merge -- but it scopes itself to FLOAT clamps and records an explicit INTEGER NEGATIVE. That negative is real but concerns a DIFFERENT transformation, and reading it as a blanket integer exclusion would have closed this axis before it was tried. Distinguish the two directions: the float law's subject is REMOVING a `cror`+`bne` pair that MWCC must build to negate an unordered-safe float compare, and there the integer case fails because negating an integer compare is already free (a single `bge`), so there is nothing to remove and the rewrite buys nothing. THIS law's subject is the opposite direction -- GAINING the ternary's empty-arm `b` that target has and you lack. That gain does not depend on the operand type at all, because it comes from the front end's block-materialisation rule for ternary arms, not from compare negation. The tell is correspondingly different: read `target-only: +N b +N beq  ours-only: -N bne` (a branch the target has and you lack), not the float law's `target-only +1 b +1 ble  ours-only -1 cror -1 bne`.

SCREEN THIS BEFORE THE EMPTY-BODIED-IF FORM, WHICH IS A TRAP. The intuitive cure for a target `beq`+`b` pair is `if (c) { } else { v = 0; }`, and it is a guaranteed null: claim.law.IT_empty-bodied-if-elides-its-own-comparison.20260901.v1 establishes that MWCC's front end discards a syntactically empty conditional body whole -- comparison, operand loads and all -- so the shape never reaches the instruction stream. The ternary is the form that works precisely because a ternary arm block is materialised where an empty statement block is not. The two laws are complements and should be read together.

PRECONDITION, and it is load-bearing: the pair must be the FORWARD variant per claim.law.empty-block-branch-pair-splits-forward-vs-backedge.20260831.v1 -- the unconditional `b` must target a merge point ahead of it, not a loop backedge. The backedge variant is folded to one inverted conditional by MWCC everywhere in this image and is not source-reachable. Check the branch targets, not just the opcode run.

ARBITRATE ON FUZZY, NOT ON real OR ON COUNT. The rewrite ADDS one instruction per site, so on a function with a large site population it will overshoot target's instruction count and can regress `real` even while the structure strictly converges. Here 24 sites took the count from 574 to 620 against a target of 611, and the companion arm-swap pass returned an explicit CONFLICT verdict (real 939 -> 947, multiset 97t -> 91t) that arbitrated to a KEEP on fresh-report fuzzy (+1.90 points). Apply claim.law.fuzzy-can-underweight-a-real-improvement.20260830.v1 and take fuzzy from a FRESH full report build; reverting either step on `real` would have discarded the entire 2.24-point gain.

COST NOTE. The ternary form asks the allocator to keep the assigned variable live across the merge, which on a register-pressured function is paid in copies: this function's ours-only copy population rose from 19 `addi` to 23 `addi` + 15 `mr` as the branch population closed. That is a real and separate residual (here it resolves to a spill-residency question), not a reason to reject the lever -- the branch structure is the thing that was source-reachable, and it closed.
